albums.blurb: Jaga Jazzist is a Norwegian large ensemble — roughly ten players, led by multi-instrumentalist Lars Horntveth — that folds horns, vibraphone, guitars, and electronics into tightly composed instrumental music. A Livingroom Hush, their second album, was the one that carried them beyond Norway when Ninja Tune picked it up internationally, and it remains the entry point to their catalog: all ten tracks are fully instrumental, splitting the difference between big-band jazz and post-rock electronica.
albums.reception: The BBC named it the best jazz album of 2002, and AllMusic rated it four stars out of five.

albums.blurb: Multi-Love is the third album from Unknown Mortal Orchestra, the project of New Zealand-born, Portland-based songwriter and producer Ruban Nielson. Recorded largely alone in his basement studio for Jagjaguwar, it marked a turn away from the lo-fi guitar psych of the first two records toward synthesizers, disco and funk rhythms, and denser production, with lyrics drawn from a polyamorous relationship in Nielson's household that year.
albums.reception: It holds a Metacritic score of 79 and placed on multiple 2015 year-end lists, including No. 10 at NME and No. 18 at The Guardian.

albums.blurb: Big Star formed in Memphis around the songwriting partnership of Chris Bell and Alex Chilton, the latter already known as the teenage voice of the Box Tops. #1 Record, their debut for the Stax-affiliated Ardent label, applied Beatles-style melodic craft to American guitar rock and effectively drew the blueprint for what became known as power pop; Stax's collapsing distribution kept it out of stores, and the band never recovered commercially despite three now-canonical albums.
albums.reception: Contemporary reviews were strong — Billboard wrote that "every cut could be a single" — but the album sold fewer than 10,000 copies on release, and Rolling Stone later ranked it No. 474 on its 2020 list of the 500 Greatest Albums of All Time.
